exams.syllabus: Trinity Woodwind & Jazz Woodwind syllabus. Lists read from the board's official repertoire pages.
comps: Face-to-face: 3 pieces x 22 (fluency & accuracy 7, technical facility 7, communication & interpretation 8) = 66; technical work 14; supporting tests 20 (Initial-G5: any two of sight reading, aural, improvisation, musical knowledge, 10 each; G6-8: sight reading 10 + aural or improvisation 10); total 100. Pass 60-74, Merit 75-86, Distinction 87-100 (Below Pass 1: 45-59; Below Pass 2: 0-44). Per piece: Distinction 19-22, Merit 16-18, Pass 13-15. No need to pass every section. Digital technical-work pathway: 3 pieces x 22 = 66, technical work 14, overall performance 20 (=100); digital Repertoire-only pathway: 4 pieces x 25 = 100; same attainment bands. UCAS points G6 8/10/12, G7 12/14/16, G8 18/24/30 (Pass/Merit/Distinction).

Three pieces from the current repertoire list: two accompanied from Group A and one unaccompanied from Group B. At Initial-G3 one Group A piece may be a duet (upper part; duet part on a woodwind instrument, live or recorded). Own composition may replace a piece (accompanied -> Group A, unaccompanied -> Group B), comparable in demand (Initial 0.5-1 min up to G8 3.5-5 min; stave notation required G6-8; no marks for quality of composition). Flute, clarinet and saxophone candidates may swap one piece for a Jazz Woodwind piece listed for the same instrument, grade and group. Instrument rules: piccolo/alto flute, Eb/bass clarinet, cor anglais, contrabassoon only where listed (max one such piece); recorder G6-8 must play both descant and treble, only one piece on tenor/sopranino/bass; no plastic saxophones. Repeats over 4 bars not played; da capo/dal segno observed; no metronomes; memory optional (no extra marks). Accompanist supplied by candidate; backing tracks allowed to G3 face-to-face (live from G4), and at all grades digitally.

Digital exams (filmed, one continuous take, up to 3GB) offer two pathways: Technical work (3 pieces + scales/arpeggios Set A or B, or exercises, or G6-8 orchestral extracts/study, + overall performance mark) or Repertoire-only (4 pieces: at least two Group A and one Group B, 25 marks each). Digital technical work uses the same material as face-to-face (Set A/B subsets); there are no supporting tests digitally.
sections: Scales & technical work

As the classical saxophone Grade 1 exam.
Aural & other tests
As the classical saxophone Grade 1 exam (aural, improvisation, musical knowledge as above).

w06412.d: Miles Davis's 6/4 modal blues from Kind of Blue, in a Cannonball Adderley edition. Practises swing feel in triple time, blues vocabulary and improvisation.

w06413.d: Jazz ballad-style solo for saxophone with a lyrical melody and room for expression. Practises tone, phrasing and rubato.

w06414.d: Funk-style etude from a blues and funk study book. Practises syncopation, ghosted articulation and groove at a demanding tempo.

w06415.d: Parker's bebop head (1947) on the chords of 'Back Home Again in Indiana', with fast chromatic lines and written-out solo; trains bebop articulation and finger agility.

w06416.d: Bebop head by Parker over 'I Got Rhythm' changes, with written-out improvisation. Practises fast bebop phrasing, accuracy and swung articulation.

w06417.d: Jazz-education tune with a head and one chorus of improvisation. Practises blues or standard changes, motif development and swing feel.

w06418.d: Blues in the style of Charlie Parker, played as written without improvisation. Practises bebop phrasing, chromatic approach notes and swing.

w06419.d: Contemporary jazz piece for saxophone, taking its title from the Powell and Pressburger film. Practises expressive phrasing and rhythmic flexibility.

w06420.d: Jazz tune in Parker's style from an improvisation book, with head then improvised solo. Practises bebop vocabulary, fluent articulation and chord-based improvisation.

w06421.d: Blues for alto saxophone with variations on the form. Practises blues scale, swing phrasing and simple improvisation.

w06422.d: First movement of a jazz-influenced sonata for alto sax and piano, played without piano improvisation. Practises wide-ranging lines, rhythmic drive and tonal control.

w06423.d: Third movement of a jazz sonata for soprano or tenor sax, with improvisation. Practises fast, rhythmically driven figures and modern harmony.

w06424.d: Fast, dense jazz study for solo sax with rapid note groupings. Practises finger speed, rhythmic accuracy and stamina without accompaniment.

w06425.d: Funk-style solo study with a groovy bass-like feel. Practises syncopation, articulation and rhythmic stamina.

w06426.d: Contemporary etude with angular, fast figures and metre changes. Practises rhythmic precision, agility and wide leaps.

w06427.d: Choice of two modern studies for solo sax in jazz, funk and rock styles. Practises technical fluency, articulation and rhythmic accuracy.

w06428.d: Spicy modern étude for solo sax with jazz-rock lines. Practises quick articulation, chromatic passagework and rhythmic drive.

w06429.d: Playful saxophone piece with see-sawing figures from a scorchers collection. Practises rapid alternation, agility and clear articulation.

w06430.d: Study in modal and diminished sounds for solo sax, played without backing. Practises unusual scales, fluency and phrase shaping.

z00312.d: Jazz saxophone pieces by Norton (Puppet Theatre or Hot Potato) in light jazz style. Practises swing feel, articulation and syncopation.
